mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 63 AMG M156 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M156 is a masterpiece of engineering, but early engines have a critical weakness: cylinder head bolt failure [1†L20-L23][11†L39-L40]. Camshaft adjuster wear is also common [1†L32-L35]. Head bolt failure affects pre-2011 M156 engines - check engine serial number [4†L37-L38]. Symptoms: coolant loss, white smoke, misfire on cold start [4†L7-L10]. Preventative head bolt upgrade costs £2,800-£4,000 at an AMG specialist [4†L11-L15]. Camshaft adjuster rattle on startup indicates wear [1†L32-L35]. With head bolts addressed, the M156 is a robust and rewarding engine.

mainEntity.name: What is the M156 head bolt problem on the Mercedes CLS 63 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M156 engine uses torque-to-yield cylinder head bolts that can stretch and snap under extreme heat and pressure [11†L39-L46][4†L12-L15]. When a bolt fails, coolant can leak into the combustion chamber [4†L7-L10]. Affects pre-2011 M156 engines up to serial number 60658 [4†L37-L38]. Symptoms: unexplained coolant loss, misfire on cold start, white smoke. If ignored, hydro-lock can bend connecting rods and write off the engine. Preventative head bolt upgrade with ARP or Weistec studs is strongly recommended [4†L11-L15]. Specialist preventative work costs £2,800-£4,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the M157 engine in the CLS 63 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M157 twin-turbo V8 is generally more reliable than the M156, but it has known weaknesses: timing chain tensioner failure and high-pressure fuel pump failure [2†L15-L17][8†L25-L27]. Timing chain rattle on cold start is common - don't ignore it [2†L35]. Install non-return valves and updated tensioners as preventative maintenance [2†L16-L17]. HPFP failure causes misfires and power loss under load [12†L6-L9]. Cylinder wall scoring can occur in some units [2†L21-L23]. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: How much does timing chain replacement cost on a Mercedes CLS 63 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timing chain replacement on a CLS 63 AMG M157 engine costs £2,500-£3,800 at a specialist or £3,500-£5,000 at a main dealer. This is preventative work. If the chain has already slipped, full engine replacement at £6,000-£7,500 is required. Specialist preventative chain replacement: £2,500-£3,800. Dealer pricing for same work: £3,500-£5,000. Rattling noise on cold start is the early warning sign [2†L35]. Once timing jumps, valves contact pistons - engine is beyond repair.

CLS 63 AMG values are stable and, in some cases, rising - they are modern classics. A clean, well-maintained CLS 63 AMG is worth saving. Rebuilt M156/M157 engines cost £6,500-£12,000 supply only. mainEntity.name: Mercedes CLS 63 AMG M156 vs M157 - which engine is more reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M157 is generally considered more reliable than the M156, but both have their weaknesses. The M156 has the well-documented head bolt failure [1†L20-L23], while the M157 suffers from timing chain tensioner and HPFP issues [2†L15-L17][8†L25-L27]. M156 (2006-2011): legendary naturally aspirated V8, but head bolt failure is a critical concern [1†L20-L23]. M157 (2011-2017): more power and torque, twin-turbo, generally more reliable but has timing chain and fuel system weaknesses [8†L25-L27]. The M156 is more rewarding to drive and listen to; the M157 is faster and more refined. Both engines are expensive to maintain and repair - budget accordingly.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLS 63 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLS 63 AMG represents the pinnacle of CLS performance across two generations. The first-generation C219 (2006-2011) was powered by the M156 6.2-litre naturally aspirated V8 - AMG's first entirely in-house designed engine, producing up to 525 hp. The second-generation C218 (2011-2017) introduced the M157 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8, delivering up to 585 hp and 800 Nm of torque in S-Model guise, cementing the CLS 63 AMG's reputation as one of the most potent four-door coupés ever built.

milestones.description: C219 CLS 63 AMG launched with M156 E63 6.2L naturally aspirated V8, 507-525 hp, 630 Nm, 7G-TRONIC
M156 production ends; replaced by M157 twin-turbo V8
C218 CLS 63 AMG launched with M157 DEH55 LA 5.5L twin-turbo V8, 525 hp, 700 Nm, AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 7-speed
CLS 63 AMG S-Model introduced with 557-585 hp, 4MATIC option
CLS 63 AMG Shooting Brake (X218) estate body style introduced
CLS 63 AMG S 4MATIC with 585 hp, 800 Nm, 0-62 mph in 3.6 seconds
C218 CLS production ends; CLS 63 AMG replaced by CLS 53 AMG MHEV

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLS 63 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLS 63 AMG is powered by two of AMG's most celebrated V8 engines - the naturally aspirated M156 and the twin-turbo M157. The M156 is a masterpiece of engineering, but early engines suffer from head bolt failure - a well-documented issue that can write off engines if ignored. The M157 is generally more robust but has timing chain tensioner and high-pressure fuel pump weaknesses. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M156 Head Bolt Failure - The CLS 63 AMG's Defining Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M156 uses torque-to-yield cylinder head bolts that can stretch and snap under extreme heat and pressure. When a bolt fails, coolant can leak into the combustion chamber, causing misfires, white smoke, and in severe cases, hydro-lock that bends connecting rods and writes off the engine. Engines up to serial number 60658 are considered at risk.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all head bolts with upgraded ARP or Weistec studs
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-60k miles; prevents catastrophic failure; the best insurance policy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cylinder head(s), head gaskets, bolts, machine heads if warped
repairOptions.longevity: Required if head bolt failure has caused damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt M156 with upgraded head bolts, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if hydro-lock has bent connecting rods

problems.recommendation: Head bolt failure is the single most significant issue affecting the M156 engine. If you own a CLS 63 AMG, preventative head bolt replacement with ARP or Weistec studs is strongly recommended. Don't wait for symptoms - coolant loss and misfires are signs that damage has already occurred. For cars with existing engine damage, a rebuilt unit with upgraded head bolts is the only safe option. This is not a DIY job - use an AMG specialist.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M156 Mercedes CLS 63 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: M157 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Rattling Noise on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The M157 timing chain tensioners can lose hydraulic pressure when the engine is stood, causing a rattling or "bag of nails" noise on cold start. If ignored, the chain can stretch and jump, causing catastrophic valve/piston contact. Installing non-return valves and updated chain tensioners is a common preventative measure.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Timing Chain Tensioner & Non-Return Valve Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioners and install non-return valves
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; cold start rattle only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, guides and sprockets. Engine-out job
repairOptions.longevity: Required if persistent rattle or chain stretch is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M157 with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped and valve damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: Rattling on cold start is the early warning sign. Don't ignore it - specialist timing chain tensioner replacement with non-return valves at £500-£900 resolves the issue if done promptly. If the chain has already slipped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M157 Mercedes CLS 63 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: M157 High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure - Misfires and Power Loss
problems.rootCause: The M157 uses two high-pressure fuel pumps (HPFPs) mounted in the engine bay. Failure of one or both pumps can cause fuel pressure drop under load, leading to misfires, power loss, and limp mode. Symptoms include hesitation under hard acceleration and the engine entering limp mode, with issues often resolving after a restart.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty HPFP with OEM Bosch unit
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; one pump failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both HPFPs, all injectors, fuel rail pressure sensor
repairOptions.longevity: Required if pump debris has contaminated the fuel system

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M157 with new fuel system components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if fuel system debris has caused bottom-end damage

problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the M157 is serious but rarely requires a full engine unless ignored. Replace the pump at the first sign of hesitation or misfiring under load. If you continue driving, fuel dilution can wipe out bearings. On a CLS 63 AMG, a specialist HPFP replacement is strong value and should be paired with a fuel system inspection.

problems.h4: M156 Camshaft Adjuster Wear - Rattling Noise on Startup
problems.rootCause: The M156 camshaft adjusters can wear, causing a rattling or clattering noise on startup. The locking pin can wear, allowing the camshaft to move out of position momentarily. If ignored, the issue can progress to timing errors and performance loss.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; rattle only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace camshaft adjusters, timing chain, tensioners, guides
repairOptions.longevity: Required if persistent rattle or timing errors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M156 with upgraded camshaft components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if camshaft adjuster wear has caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: Rattling on startup is the early warning sign. Don't ignore it - specialist camshaft adjuster replacement at £1,800-£2,800 resolves the issue if done promptly. If the rattle has been present for months, the chain and guides may also be worn, requiring a full timing overhaul.
